sections.Profile:
Jungle , Wild Life , and Jungle King are pinball machines produced by D. Gottlieb & Co. in the early 1970s, all designed by Ed Krynski with artwork by Gordon Morison. These machines share a jungle theme and feature similar gameplay mechanics, including rollovers that advance the bonus, a kickback in the left outlane, and a gate at the right outlane. The main differences lie in their player capacities and bonus rules: Jungle is a four-player game produced in 1972 with a focus on doubling bonuses on the last ball; Wild Life is a two-player version with similar rules; and Jungle King is a single-player "add-a-ball" version released in 1973, allowing for bonus doubling on every ball under specific conditions.
